newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Cargo ship docking with Mir station successful.
newsitem.headline: Cargo ship docking with Mir station successful.

text.p: A supply ship docked with Russia's Mir space station on Monday, delivering equipment crucial for the future of the troubled 11-year mission.
"Contact," a mission control official said amid applause in the control centre at Korolyov near Moscow, where senior government and space industry officials were present for the tricky docking.
Officials said the fully automatic docking operation finished successfully after six minutes from the first contact.

"All electric connections between Mir and Progress have been made. Tightening of the connection has been carried out," the official said, adding that this was the final stage of the docking operation.
Officials said the sprawling space station was directly over the Volga river in Russia on its orbit round the Earth when the docking took place.

"Don't do anything before the next radio contact," Vladimir Solovyov, the flight director, told Mir crew during a radio contact which continued through all phases of the docking. The next contact was due within an hour's time.
Officials said three docking attempts had been envisaged in the case of problems.
The predecessor of the unmanned Progress craft launched on Saturday crashed into the station during docking on June 25 in the worst accident in the station's history.
Mir lost up to half its electric power in the collision and experts had said this could hamper Monday's docking.

The latest Progress craft is carrying oxygen, food and water as well as the tools needed to save the station. There are also parcels from the families of the three-man Russian-U.S. crew, who have had a nerve-wracking and uncomfortable time since the accident.
